title: Continuous span and shape at a 1 N·m torque budget, 0.5 mm FAAV sheet
author: sam
question: With half-span free to move in 10 mm steps and chords refined to 5 mm, what single half-span and outline give the most thrust under a 1 N·m peak-torque budget for the FAAV sheet (0.5 mm, pivoting on a stiff leading edge) at 1 Hz, and how much thrust is lost by staying within the 400 mm single-sheet manufacturing limit?
notes: Boundary condition: the FAAV build. A 0.5 mm carbon sheet on a stiff leading edge that the sheet pivots about; the leading edge itself neither bends nor twists. That is the chordwise t0.50 model: the leading edge is held straight and in place, each strip pitches about it against the sheet's own torsion and warping, root fixed to the hub; the rod is not modelled (its torsion excluded, its mass on the pitch axis). Lineages: the seven per-span winners of the parent study plus 28 family seeds (4 families x 7 half-spans), so the optimum is approached from many starts. Span is a search coordinate (20 mm step, 10 mm half-step) and chords use a 10 mm step (5 mm half-step), so winners are not tied to a span grid. Manufacturing: a single sheet is at most 400 mm, so half-spans above 400 mm need a joined sheet; the search is not limited to it, the atlas shades the zone.
